steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The HR diagram plots luminosity (vertical axis, increasing upward) against temperature/spectral class (horizontal axis, decreasing left to right)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The main sequence runs diagonally from top-left (hot, luminous) to bottom-right (cool, dim)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Red giants appear in the upper-right: cool but very luminous due to large size

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: White dwarfs appear in the lower-left: hot but dim due to small size

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What are the axes of the HR diagram? | Q: Where are white dwarfs found on the HR diagram and why? | Q: Why are red giants luminous despite being cool?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Vertical axis: luminosity or absolute magnitude (increasing upward). Horizontal axis: temperature or spectral class (decreasing left to right — hot stars on the left). | Lower-left: they are hot (high temperature) but dim (low luminosity) because they are very small. | Because they have enormous surface area — luminosity depends on both temperature and radius (L ∝ R²T⁴), so a very large radius compensates for low temperature.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Temperature axis goes BACKWARDS (right to left) — hot on left, cool on right — this catches many students out Know the three main regions: main sequence, giant branch, white dwarf region The Sun is on the main sequence — be able to mark its position Both boards test HR diagram interpretation: be prepared to identify regions and describe what they represent
